title: Incident tactical brief & customer-facing templates
content:
Purpose
This is a tactical working brief for customer-facing comms during infrastructure or inference incidents. Includes short status-page-ready text blocks, staggered update templates, a customer postmortem summary scaffold, and suggested SLA/credit language for commercial customers. Use these as starting text — keep edits minimal during an incident to avoid confusion.

Audience
Primary: customer-success managers, account managers, solutions engineers who need to post or escalate status updates. Secondary: SRE/ops for timeline facts and engineering-led postmortems.

How to use
- Pick the block that matches impact level (degraded, partial outage, full outage).
- Fill in the placeholders in ALL CAPS (e.g., {AFFECTED_REGION}, {ESTIMATED_RESTORE}).
- Keep the first public status update short (<= 3 sentences) and mark ‘investigating’.
- For targeted email to Enterprise customers, include timelines and a named escalation contact.

QUICK STATUS PAGE SNIPPETS (copy/paste)
1) Investigating — short (public status page)
Title: Degraded inference throughput for hosted-api in {REGION}
Summary: We are investigating increased request latency and timeouts affecting model inference in {REGION}. API requests may be slower or return errors. Our engineers are actively investigating.
Impact: Some requests to hosted endpoints in {REGION} may experience increased latency or errors; embeddings and admin APIs may be affected.
Next update: within 30 minutes

2) Update — mitigation in progress
Title: Mitigation deployed, monitoring for stability in {REGION}
Summary: We deployed a mitigation that routes traffic to a stable pool and applied a temporary rate adjustment. Error rates have decreased but some users may still see elevated latency.
Impact: Majority of customers are seeing restored responses; a subset of long-running / high-concurrency requests may still be impacted.
Workaround: Reduce concurrency or switch to a lower-latency model variant (e.g., {MODEL_VARIANT}).
Next update: 1 hour or sooner if conditions change

3) Resolved
Title: Service restored — hosted-api inference in {REGION}
Summary: The issue impacting inference latency and errors in {REGION} has been resolved. Normal service has resumed and we are monitoring.
Impact: All customers should see normal API behavior. If you continue to experience issues, please open a support ticket or contact your CSM.
Follow-up: A customer-facing postmortem will be published within 5 business days.

CUSTOMER EMAIL TEMPLATE — enterprise (short)
Subject: Incident update — {SHORT_ISSUE_SUMMARY} — {DATE}
Hi {CUSTOMER_NAME},
We wanted to let you know we are investigating an incident affecting {PRODUCT/ENDPOINT} in {REGION} starting at {UTC_START_TIME}. Our initial investigation shows increased request latency and intermittent errors for some workloads.
What we are doing: Engineers have applied a traffic routing mitigation to reduce impact and are monitoring KPIs (latency, error rate, request throughput).
Estimated next update: {ETA}
Your account contact: {CSM_NAME} ({CSM_EMAIL}) — available for any escalation.
We will follow up with a detailed post-incident summary.
Thanks for your patience,
{REDACTED_SIGNATURE}

DETAILED POST-INCIDENT CUSTOMER SUMMARY (5-part scaffold)
1) Executive summary (1–3 sentences)
- What happened: brief description in customer language (no internal jargon).
- Impact: who was affected and how (examples: higher latency, dropped responses, failing embeddings).
- Customer-facing resolution: what customers should expect now.

2) Timeline (chronological, UTC times)
- {UTC_TIME} — anomaly detected by monitoring (metric and threshold).
- {UTC_TIME} — incident declared; page status set to investigating.
- {UTC_TIME} — mitigation X deployed (traffic routing / scaling / model fallback).
- {UTC_TIME} — error rates decreased to baseline.
- {UTC_TIME} — service marked resolved; postmortem initiated.
Note: Avoid internal ticket IDs in public timeline unless they help the customer.

3) Root cause (clear and non‑blameful)
- High-level cause statement: e.g., "root cause: an interaction between request routing and KV-cache eviction that caused persistent worker overload in a subset of GPU pools."
- Contributing factors: list 2–4 items (capacity thresholds, an outdated autoscaling policy, an incorrect kernel selection profile).

4) Customer impact and scope
- Affected services: hosted API inference (text-gen and embeddings), region(s), percentage of requests/customers impacted (if known).
- Mitigations customers might have used or can use in future (model fallback, reduced concurrency, cached responses).

5) Corrective actions and timeline
- Short-term: applied routing mitigation and temporary autoscale increase (completed at {UTC_TIME}).
- Mid-term (2–7 days): roll out kernel selector fix and a canary of the autoscaler change; update status page when complete.
- Long-term: change default autoscale thresholds, introduce per-tenant soft-limits, add a regression test in CI for KV-cache interaction.
- Customer compensation: we will evaluate SLA credits per the contract and notify affected customers within 10 business days.

Suggested SLA/credit language (customer-facing)
If you are eligible under your contract for an SLA credit, we will calculate the affected usage window and apply any credit per the terms of your agreement. Your CSM will follow up with specifics for your account.

Escalation contact lines (include personalized contact for accounts)
- Primary CS contact: {CSM_NAME}, {CSM_EMAIL}, {CSM_PHONE}
- 24x7 engineering pager (for enterprise agreements): eng-pager@redwood.example (include incident ref)

SHORT FAQ (for status page or email expansion)
Q: Will my data be exposed?
A: No evidence of data exfiltration was found. All input/output logs are retained per our retention policy and will be reviewed as part of the postmortem.
Q: What should I do now?
A: If you are experiencing errors, try reducing concurrency or switching to a compatible model variant; contact your CSM if this is not possible.
Q: When will the postmortem be published?
A: A customer-facing postmortem will be available within 5 business days and a technical postmortem will be shared internally.

MESSAGE VARIATIONS FOR DIFFERENT TONES
- Short and neutral (public-facing): "Investigating increased latency in {REGION}. We are working on a mitigation and will update soon."
- Proactive & reassuring (enterprise email): "We applied a targeted routing change that reduced error rates by X%. We remain on heightened watch and will keep you informed every hour."
- Technical addendum (for partner/account teams): include specific hashes, model variants, and the JIRA ticket for deeper troubleshooting.

REVIEW CHECKLIST BEFORE PUBLISHING
- [ ] Timeline times verified by SRE
- [ ] Statement reviewed by legal if data/exposure is mentioned
- [ ] CSM for affected accounts notified and copied
- [ ] Engineering-approved resolution language (no unsourced claims)
- [ ] SLA/credit mention matches contract team guidance

WORKING NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS (for authors)
- Decide whether to include percent of customers impacted or keep qualitative wording. Use percentages only if metrics are reliable.
- Confirm whether embeddings API is affected separately; sometimes embeddings pipelines run on different pools.
- Draft for translation/localization if region has non-English enterprise customers.

EDIT HISTORY
- 2026-03-11 — initial draft by Aisha Patel (status snippets, enterprise email, postmortem scaffold).
- 2026-03-12 — added SLA language and review checklist (Marcus Reed).

CONTACT
For feedback on templates or to add a canned phrase: ping #cs-templates or contact Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.example).

END OF BRIEF
